relevance_reason: The paper reports patients with heterozygous ESRRG variants and a non-progressive congenital movement disorder with ataxia and eye movement disorders, with functional studies. This is the defining report for CONMAE.

findings.statement: Bresack et al. (2025) described 8 individuals from 7 unrelated families with a non-progressive congenital movement disorder with ataxia. All had motor developmental delay, muscular hypotonia, eye movement disorders, and congenital ataxia or gait imbalance. Other features included joint hyperflexibility, dysarthria, myopia, and growth delay.
quotes: We clinically describe eight individuals from seven unrelated families having heterozygous, mostly de novo variants in ESRRG

All individuals have motor developmental delay, muscular hypotonia, and eye movement disorders, as well as congenital ataxia or gait imbalance. Other symptoms include joint hyperflexibility, dysarthria, myopia, and growth delay.

findings.statement: Bresack et al. (2025) found heterozygous ESRRG variants, most of them de novo, in the affected individuals. This is consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance.
quotes: having heterozygous, mostly de novo variants in ESRRG
Genetic variants in ESRRG are associated with a dominant non-progressive congenital movement disorder with ataxia.

findings.statement: Bresack et al. (2025) identified a heterozygous c.410G>A (p.Gly137Glu) variant in ESRRG in a patient with a non-progressive congenital movement disorder with ataxia. The variant was absent from gnomAD v4.1, predicted deleterious in silico, and located in an intolerant segment of the protein. It showed reduced transcriptional activity in an ERRE reporter assay and failed to restore proliferation in ESRRG-knockout HEK293T cells.
quotes: All identified variants are absent in gnomAD (v.4.1), are in silico deleterious, and are located in intolerant segments of the protein.

findings.statement: Bresack et al. (2025) found that ESRRG knockout significantly increased the proliferation rate of HEK293T cells. Wild-type ESRRG restored normal proliferation, but none of the patient variants did. All variants localized correctly to the nucleus but significantly reduced transcriptional activity in an ERRE reporter assay. Molecular modeling also suggested reduced protein function.
quotes: ESRRG knockout resulted in a significantly increased proliferation rate in ESRRG-knockout HEK293T cells. Overexpression of wild-type ESRRG restored cell proliferation, while overexpression of the identified variants did not.
Despite the correct nuclear localization of all identified variants, the reporter gene assay revealed a significant reduction in transcriptional activity for all identified variants.
Molecular modeling of the identified variants suggests a reduction in protein function.
